the species variability observed in plasma S-sul-fonate levels during sulfite administration is a function of the relative availability of sulfite to plasma protein and the rate of sulfite metabolism.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
sulfite reacts with reactive disulfide groups to form S-sulfonated protein.
sulfite reacts with plasma protein disulfide bonds, forming S-sulfonated proteins, which are stable for a long time.
sulfite is metabolized by the rat, mouse, rabbit, and rhesus, but the extent of sulfite utilization is dependent on the species.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the plasma levels of S-sulfonated proteins are species dependent.
the plasma protein S-sul-fonate fraction is a potentially useful indicator of the availability of sulfites to the body.
